base_member_text: [L430-L442] (MED/singular factorization) The SIP factorization divides by 1+p1, 1+p2, and p3 without singularity checks; adding a fixed small value to p3 does not prevent exact or near cancellation.
audit_member_text: [L430-L442] (MED/unchecked factorization denominator) SIP divides by 1+p1, 1+p2, and p3 without finite/near-zero checks; adding a fixed 1e-15 only to p3 does not protect the first two denominators or scale with the matrix.

adversarial.rationale: The unchecked denominators are real, but failure requires a singular/poorly scaled factorization or loss of the usual favorable matrix structure. The nonhydrostatic slope terms do not provide a universal pivot bound, while small added only to p3 leaves 1+p1 and 1+p2 entirely unprotected; this is a numerical robustness defect rather than evidence that ordinary SIP solves fail.

base_member_text: [L427-L460,L467-L510] (MED/zero-right-hand-side convergence) When bnorm is zero, epslin remains exactly zero and the strict rnorm<epslin test cannot succeed even for an exactly zero residual, forcing all maxit iterations.
audit_member_text: [L427-L460,L467-L510] (MED/false nonconvergence) For bnorm=0 the convergence threshold is exactly zero and the strict rnorm<epslin test can never pass even for an exact zero residual, forcing maxit iterations and recording nonconvergence.

adversarial.rationale: For a zero RHS the relative threshold is zero, and an exactly solved zero residual fails the strict less-than comparison. There is no absolute tolerance or zero-RHS early return before the iteration loop, so even this converged case can exhaust the configured iterations.

audit_member_text: [L113-L121,L186-L216] (MED/solver selection contract) solver_init marks the module initialized even when par%solver matches neither supported branch, after which solver_solvemat silently performs no solve.

adversarial.rationale: params.F90:882-889 restricts the solver to sip or tridiag through the validated option reader. Invalid option strings halt before solver_solvemat is called, so the missing fallback branch is not reachable from supported configuration input.

base_member_text: [L109-L121,L186-L216] (MED/configuration lifecycle) Solver parameters and workspace shape are captured only on the first initialization; repeated initialization can double-allocate, while later solves with changed dimensions or parameters silently reuse the old state.
audit_member_text: [L109-L121,L186-L216] (MED/state/configuration lifecycle) Solver settings and array dimensions are captured only on the first initialization, with no protection against a later call using changed nx, ny, solver choice, or solver parameters.

adversarial.rationale: The saved dimensions and solver settings can become incompatible only on reuse with changed grid/configuration or an external parameter change. They remain consistent throughout an ordinary fixed-configuration run, but neither solver_solvemat nor solver_free implements the required reinitialization for that later lifecycle.

base_member_text: [L285-L299] (HIGH/singular pivot) The Thomas solver divides by each pivot with no protection in its normal caller; the optional fix is not passed, and even when enabled it only catches values below machine tiny rather than numerically small pivots.
audit_member_text: [L285-L299] (MED/unchecked zero pivot) The Thomas solver divides by each pivot while the normal caller omits fixshallow, so zero or near-zero pivots are not guarded.

adversarial.rationale: The normal nonhydrostatic caller omits fixshallow, so zero or near-zero elimination pivots remain unchecked for degenerate or poorly conditioned matrices; the wet-cell identity rows do not constrain all active slope-dependent rows. Groundwater callers explicitly enabling fixshallow do have a tiny-pivot replacement, so this is not a universal failure of every Thomas call.
